findings.title: Use the underlying IdP state when deciding whether to invalidate login caches
findings.body: `update()` obtains `original` through `getById()`, which returns an organization-aware model whose `isEnabled()` is false whenever its organization is disabled. If a cached, enabled public organization IdP is updated from `BROKER_PUBLIC=true` to `false` while that organization is disabled, the predicate is false for both `original` (because the organization is disabled) and `updated` (because the IdP is now private), so this code skips invalidation. Once the organization is enabled, the cached ID remains in `getForLogin()` results and its model reports enabled, exposing a broker that is no longer public. Compare the underlying IdP eligibility independently of organization enabled state, or invalidate when the public setting changes.

findings.title: Cleanup callbacks target the literal alias instead of the created providers
findings.body: This cleanup registration uses `get("alias")` rather than the created provider's alias. The loop creates providers named `idp-alias-0` through `idp-alias-19`, so its callbacks target the same unrelated alias instead of removing those providers; the added cleanup for `idp-alias-20` has the same problem. The test therefore leaves its created IdPs behind (and may issue deletes for a nonexistent provider), risking test contamination.
